title: Manual Blending, Perspective Warp, and Sunrise Color Grading in Landscape Post-Processing
summary: This tutorial-style video presents two manual approaches to correcting mistakes and blending exposures after a focus stack in landscape photography. The workflow emphasizes perspective adjustment using perspective warp and the rule of trapezoids, edge alignment via edge-colored cloning with a very small brush, puppet warp for composition control, and iterative color/tonal grading to simulate a sunrise. The presenter demonstrates RAW adjustments, selective masking, shadow dodging, and staged color grading (warmth, blues, and Orton-style glow), along with notes on plugin usage (Topaz) and creating HDR-like results through layered processing. The process is shown as a practical, field-editable workflow with attention to horizon alignment, edge seamlessness, and guiding the viewer’s eye toward the light source.

sections.title: Manual edge blending and alignment

sections.title: Warping, color matching, and initial processing

sections.title: Sunrise color grading and light shaping
sections.description: Details iterative warming and cool balancing to simulate a sunrise, including glow and tonal adjustments.

sections.title: Workflow acceleration, sky cleanup, and HDR-like blends
sections.description: Discusses faster processing, standalone Topaz usage, and creating HDR-like sky/foreground blends through selective layering and adjustments.

sections.title: Final tweaks, tilting compensation, and composition notes
sections.description: Addresses final corrections for tilt, crop decisions, and broader composition considerations given equipment constraints.
